title: Divisor topology of the wavefunction zero-locus
html:
Linking and splitting in the divisor. The zero-locus \{\psi = 0\} forms a Weil divisor. Each blowup at a ramification point replaces a zero z_i with an exceptional divisor E_i \cong \mathbb{CP}^1:

  • Splitting: A single zero resolves into multiple components E_{i_1}, \ldots, E_{i_k}. The vortex filament bifurcates and the mass decomposes as \sum_j \lambda_j|\Phi_q(z_{i_j})|, reproducing the topological decomposition.
  • Linking: The intersection E_i \cdot E_j \neq 0 in homology if and only if the corresponding vortex filaments are Hopf-linked. The intersection pairing measures the strong-force binding energy generated by the mutual velocity induction between linked filaments.

The divisor structure of \{\psi = 0\} — not the real density |\psi|^2 — correctly tracks vortex topology and particle content.
